quests.instruction: In bright sunshine, a dark shape that looks like you stretches across the sidewalk. What is it?
quests.hint: It appears when something blocks light.
quests.explanation: A shadow forms when your body blocks sunlight, so the light cannot reach the ground behind you.
quests.funFact: Your shadow changes shape when you move your arms or legs.

quests.instruction: On which day would you see the clearest shadow?
quests.hint: Shadows need strong light to look sharp.
quests.explanation: Direct sunlight makes sharp, dark shadows. On cloudy days, light is spread out, so shadows look faint.
quests.funFact: People have used shadows for thousands of years to tell time with sundials.

quests.instruction: Streetlights flicker on along the road, one after another. What is happening to the sky?
quests.hint: Streetlights help people when there is not enough natural light.
quests.explanation: Many streetlights have sensors that turn them on when the sky gets dark, so people can see at dusk and night.
quests.funFact: The first streetlights were lit by hand using gas or oil lamps.

quests.instruction: Which colors do we often see in the sky near sunset?
quests.hint: The Sun is low and its light has a long way to go through the air.
quests.explanation: Near sunset, sunlight passes through more air, so we see warm colors like orange and pink.
quests.funFact: The same sky colors can also appear at sunrise.

quests.instruction: When the Sun is low in the sky, how do shadows look?
quests.hint: Imagine the light coming from the side instead of overhead.
quests.explanation: When the Sun is low, light hits objects from the side, so shadows stretch out long behind them.
quests.funFact: Early morning and late afternoon give you your longest shadows of the day.

quests.instruction: Where can you see stars most clearly?
quests.correctAnswer: A dark field far from city lights
options: A dark field far from city lights
quests.hint: Bright lights wash out faint ones.
quests.explanation: Stars show up best in a dark place, because bright lights nearby make it harder for our eyes to see faint stars.
quests.funFact: Far from cities, thousands of stars can be seen on a clear night.

quests.instruction: More and more stars appear in the sky as time passes after sunset. Why?
quests.hint: Consider what is slowly disappearing after sunset.
quests.explanation: After sunset, the light fades, so the sky becomes darker and more stars become visible.
quests.funFact: Most stars are too faint to see until the sky is truly dark.

quests.instruction: A classroom turns on its lights during a dark, stormy afternoon. Why?
quests.hint: It is still day, so what could dim the light?
quests.explanation: Thick storm clouds can block much of the sunlight, so a day can feel dim even though the Sun is still up.
quests.funFact: Rain clouds can be several kilometers thick, which is why they look dark underneath.

quests.instruction: The Sun climbs higher in the sky and the sky grows brighter. Which part of the day is moving along?
quests.hint: The Sun is getting higher, not lower.
quests.explanation: As the Sun climbs higher after sunrise, morning light grows stronger.
quests.funFact: Sunlight reaches us from about 150 million kilometers away.

quests.instruction: Moonlight is really...
options: Light the Moon makes by itself
quests.hint: The Moon is a rock, not a star.
quests.explanation: The Moon does not make its own light. It reflects sunlight, which is why we can see it glowing in the night sky.
quests.funFact: The Moon is about a quarter the width of Earth.

quests.instruction: What do we call it when the Sun first appears at the start of the day?
quests.hint: One of these words means the Sun is arriving.
quests.explanation: Sunrise is when the Sun first appears above the horizon, starting the day.
quests.funFact: Sunrise happens in a slightly different spot on the horizon throughout the year.

quests.instruction: The sky was bright blue at lunchtime. What might it look like around sunset?
quests.hint: Ask yourself how the sky changes as the Sun gets lower.
quests.explanation: As the Sun gets lower, sunlight takes a longer path through air, so the blue fades and warm colors appear.
quests.funFact: Clouds can look pink, orange, or purple at sunset because they catch the low light.

quests.instruction: Which of these still gives light after the Sun has gone down?
quests.hint: Which one depends on the Sun?
quests.explanation: Streetlamps make their own light, so they glow even when the Sun is not in our sky.
quests.funFact: Streetlamps often use LED bulbs, which use less electricity than older bulbs.

quests.instruction: Dusk is the time when the sky turns dim after sunset. Which sky fits dusk?
quests.correctAnswer: Fading glow with the first stars
options: Fading glow with the first stars
Bright blue with the Sun overhead
quests.hint: Dusk happens when light is leaving.
quests.explanation: Dusk is the dim, fading-light time after sunset, when the first stars may start to appear.
quests.funFact: Sometimes the first bright dot you see at dusk is not a star but a planet, such as Venus.

quests.instruction: Rita's shadow was short at lunchtime. Later it grew very long. What changed?
quests.correctAnswer: The Sun got lower in the sky
options: The Sun got lower in the sky
The Sun got higher in the sky
quests.hint: Long shadows come from low light.
quests.explanation: As the Sun sinks lower in the sky, it lights things from the side, so shadows get longer.
quests.funFact: Sundials work because the shadow of a stick moves around as the Sun seems to move.

quests.instruction: A cloudy afternoon looks dim. Is that the same as night?
quests.correctAnswer: No, the Sun is still up
options: Yes, clouds turn day into night
No, the Sun is still up
quests.hint: Clouds can only block light, not remove the Sun.
quests.explanation: Clouds block some sunlight and make the day dim. The Sun is still shining above them, so it is still day.
quests.funFact: Even on a cloudy day, you can still get sunburned because some sunlight gets through.

quests.instruction: When do we usually see the longest shadows of the day?
quests.hint: The Sun is lowest at the very start and end of daylight.
quests.explanation: Shadows stretch out most when the Sun is low, which happens soon after sunrise and just before sunset.
quests.funFact: Shadows are shortest when the Sun is at its highest point in the sky.

quests.instruction: Why can we not see most stars during the day?
options: The stars have all moved away
quests.hint: The stars are still there. Something else is in the way.
quests.explanation: Stars are always in the sky, but the bright light of the Sun fills our sky and hides most of them.
quests.funFact: Our Sun is bright enough that it outshines every other star in our sky.

quests.instruction: A night-light is small. What is its job?
quests.correctAnswer: Give a soft glow in the dark
options: Give a soft glow in the dark
quests.hint: Tiny lights do small jobs.
quests.explanation: A night-light gives a gentle glow so you can find your way in a dark room without being too bright to sleep.
quests.funFact: Many night-lights are shaped like animals or stars.

quests.instruction: Birds begin singing, and the sky behind the mountains turns pale gold. Which part of the day is it?
quests.hint: Birds are just waking up.
quests.explanation: Birds singing and pale gold light mean the day is just starting. Many birds sing a lot around sunrise.
quests.funFact: Many bird songs are loudest at sunrise, a time people call the dawn chorus.

quests.instruction: Which of these often turns on by itself when it gets dark outside?
quests.hint: Some lights have special sensors that check the sunlight.
quests.explanation: Many streetlights have light sensors, so they switch on when it gets dark and off when it is bright again.
quests.funFact: Some streetlights use solar panels to save energy collected during the day.

quests.instruction: A girl stands on the beach as the Sun touches the sea. Her family has been swimming all day and is packing up. Is the Sun rising or setting?
quests.hint: Notice what the family has been doing all day.
quests.explanation: The family has played all day and is packing up, so the Sun is setting, ending the daylight.
quests.funFact: Sunsets over the sea are often red and orange in color.

quests.instruction: What happens to the sky between sunset and midnight?
quests.correctAnswer: It goes from dim to dark
options: It goes from dark to bright
It goes from dim to dark
quests.hint: After sunset the light is leaving.
quests.explanation: After the Sun sets, the sky becomes dim and then dark, which is why the later it gets, the darker the sky.
quests.funFact: Even at midnight, the sky is dark in most places, but moonlight can make it brighter.

quests.instruction: From outside, a window glows warm yellow while the sky is dim and blue-gray. What is the most likely cause?
quests.correctAnswer: Lights are on inside the house
options: Lights are on inside the house
quests.hint: A dim sky means the Sun is not shining much.
quests.explanation: The sky is dim, so the glow is coming from lamps or ceiling lights switched on inside.
quests.funFact: Warm-colored light bulbs look yellow, while cool-colored bulbs look whiter.

quests.instruction: Which gives us almost all of the light we use during the day?
quests.hint: One is a star. One is a rock.
quests.explanation: The Sun is the star that gives us daylight and warmth. The Moon only reflects some of that light.
quests.funFact: The Sun is so large that about 1.3 million Earths could fit inside it.

quests.instruction: Why do drivers turn on headlights as evening gets dim?
quests.correctAnswer: To see the road and be seen
options: To see the road and be seen
quests.hint: Focus on safety.
quests.explanation: Headlights light the road ahead and make cars easier for others to see when the light is low.
quests.funFact: Headlights have a low beam for city streets and a high beam for dark roads.

quests.instruction: Which of these is true about stars during the day?
quests.correctAnswer: They are still there, hidden by bright sunlight
options: They disappear and come back at night
They are still there, hidden by bright sunlight
quests.hint: Light can hide things even if they are still there.
quests.explanation: Stars stay in the sky all day. The Sun's bright light just makes the sky too bright to see them.
quests.funFact: If you travel above Earth's atmosphere, you can see stars even when the Sun is shining.

quests.instruction: Which description fits late afternoon best?
quests.correctAnswer: Long shadows and a golden, low Sun
options: Long shadows and a golden, low Sun
Short shadows and a very high Sun
quests.hint: Check where the Sun is in each picture.
quests.explanation: In late afternoon the Sun is lower, so shadows grow long and the light looks golden.
quests.funFact: Photographers love late afternoon light because it is soft and warm.

quests.instruction: Which sky goes with the very start of the day?
quests.correctAnswer: Pale light spreading above the horizon
options: A deep dark sky with a bright Moon
Pale light spreading above the horizon
quests.hint: The start of the day is when the light returns.
quests.explanation: At the start of the day, soft light spreads from the horizon as the Sun gets ready to rise.
quests.funFact: The Sun is not actually moving up. Earth is turning so we see it rise.

quests.instruction: Tomas flips on the kitchen light because it is getting hard to see his drawing. What is probably happening outside?
options: The Sun is at its highest
quests.hint: Decide why a light is needed at that moment.
quests.explanation: When daylight fades, rooms get dim, so we switch on lights to see well.
quests.funFact: Reading in dim light can make your eyes feel tired, so a lamp can help.
